==English== {{wp|}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/spiːd/}} * {{audio|en|en-us-speed.ogg|a=US}} * {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-speed.wav|a=Southern England}} * {{rhymes|en|iːd|s=1}} * {{homophones|en|Speid}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*speh₁-}} From {{inh|en|enm|sped||prosperity, good luck, quickness, success}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spēd||success}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*spōdi||prosperity, success}}, from {{der|en|gmw-pro|*spōan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*spōaną||to prosper, succeed, be happy}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*speh₁-||to prosper, turn out well}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|spede}}, {{m|sco|speid||success, quickness, speed}}, {{cog|nl|spoed||haste; speed}}, {{cog|nds-de|Spood||haste; speed; eagerness; success}}, {{cog|de|Sput||progress, acceleration, haste}}. Related also to {{cog|ang|spōwan||to be successful, succeed}}, {{cog|sq|shpejt||to speed, to hurry}} and {{cog|ru|спеши́ть||to hurry}}, {{cog|la|spēs||hope, expectation}}, {{m|la|spērō||hope|pos=verb}}, perhaps also to {{cog|grc|σπεύδω||to urge on, hasten, press on}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # The state of moving quickly or the capacity for rapid motion. #: {{syn|en|celerity|rapidity|velocity|Thesaurus:speed}} #: {{ux|en|How does Usain Bolt run at that '''speed'''?}} #* {{RQ:Marlowe Tamburlaine|part=1|scene=i|page=17|passage=Returne with '''ſpeed''', time paſſeth ſwift away,
Our life is fraile, and we may dye to day.}} # {{lb|en|mathematics|physics}} The rate of motion or action, specifically the magnitude of the [[velocity]]; the rate [[distance]] is traversed in a given [[time]]. #: {{hypo|en|lightspeed|speed of light|speed of sound}} #: {{ux|en|'''Speed''' limits provide information to the drivers about the safe '''speed''' to travel in average conditions.}} # {{lb|en|photography}} The sensitivity to light of [[film]], [[plates]] or [[sensor]]. # {{lb|en|photography}} The duration of exposure, the time during which a camera shutter is open ([[shutter speed]]). # {{lb|en|photography}} The largest size of the lens opening at which a lens can be used. # {{lb|en|photography}} The ratio of the focal length to the diameter of a photographic objective. # {{senseid|en|amphetamine-especially-methamphetamine}} {{lb|en|slang|uncountable}} [[amphetamine|Amphetamine]] or any amphetamine-based drug (especially [[methamphetamine]]) used as a [[stimulant]], especially illegally. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:methamphetamine}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2021|author={{w|Paris Lees}}|title=What it Feels Like for a Girl|publisher=Penguin (2022)|page=115|passage=I don’t even like '''speed'''. It’s alright if ya wanna stay awake for three days an’ clean yer room, but I’m terrible on no sleep. It just makes me anxious.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} [[luck|Luck]], [[success]], [[prosperity]]. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Romeo and Juliet|act=V|scene=iii|page=76|passage=St. Francis be my '''ſpeed''', how oft to night / Haue my old feet ſtumbled at graues?}} #* {{RQ:KJV|Genesis|24|12|passage=O Lord God of my master Abraham, I pray thee, send me good '''speed''' this day.}} # {{senseid|en|preference}} {{lb|en|slang}} Personal [[preference]]. #: {{ux|en|We could go to the shore next week, or somewhere else if that's not your '''speed'''.}} # {{lb|en|finance|uncountable}} A [[third-order]] measure of [[derivative]] price sensitivity, expressed as the rate of change of [[gamma]] with respect to changes in the [[underlying]] [[asset]] [[price]]. #: {{syn|en|DgammaDspot|gamma of the gamma}} #: ====Interjection==== {{en-intj}} # {{lb|en|film}} Called by the [[soundman]] when the recording equipment has reached running speed and is ready to go. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2000|author=Brian J. Hayes|title=A Boy Scout in Hollywood|page=30 |passage=“'''Speed''',” Carlos, the soundman, said. {{...}}
“Camera.”
“Rolling,” replied Bryce, the cameraman.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Tom Mascaro|title=Into the Fray|page=52 |passage={{...}} the director called, “Roll 'em,” the sound man said, “'''Speed''',” and Norling stepped in and said, {{...}}}} ===Etymology 2=== From {{inh|en|enm|speden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|spēdan||to speed, prosper, succeed, have success}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*spōdijan||to succeed}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|spede}}, {{m|sco|speid||to meet with success, assist, promote, accomplish, speed}}, {{cog|nl|spoeden||to hurry, rush}}, {{cog|nds|spoden}}, {{m|nds|spöden||to hasten, speed}}, {{cog|de|sputen}}, {{m|de|spuden||to speed}}. ====Verb==== {{en-verb|~s|~ing|sped,~ed}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|archaic}} To [[succeed]]; to [[prosper]], be lucky. #* {{RQ:Mlry MrtDrthr|4.1|2|I|1|passage=And yf I maye fynde suche a knyghte that hath all these vertues / he may drawe oute this swerd oute of the shethe / for I haue ben at kyng Ryons / it was told me ther were passyng good knyghtes / and he and alle his knyghtes haue assayed it and none can '''spede'''}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|V|i|text=We have been praying for our husbands' healths,
Which '''speed''', we hope, the better for our words.
Are they returned?}} #* {{RQ:Burton Melancholy|edition=2nd|part=I|section=2|member=4|subsection=vii|passage=Aristotle must find out the motion of Euripus; Pliny must needs see Vesuvius; but how '''sped''' they? One loseth goods, another his life.}} #* '''18thc.''', {{w|Oliver Goldsmith}}, ''Introductory to Switzerland'' # {{lb|en|transitive|archaic}} To [[help]] someone, to give them fortune; to aid or favour. #: {{ux|en|God '''speed''', until we meet again.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Winter's Tale|act=IV|scene=iv|passage=Fortune '''speed''' us! So we set forth to sea}} #* {{RQ:Dryden Aeneis|passage=with rising gales that '''sped''' their happy flight}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To go [[fast]]. #: {{syn|en|zing}} #: {{ux|en|The Ferrari was '''speeding''' along the road.}} #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Henry 4-2|act=IV|scene=ii|passage=I have '''speeded''' hither with the very extremest inch of possibility.}} #* {{RQ:Allingham China Governess|chapter=10|passage=With a little manœuvring they contrived to meet on the doorstep which was {{...}} in a boiling stream of passers-by, hurrying business people '''speeding''' past in a flurry of fumes and dust in the bright haze.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To exceed the [[speed limit]]. #: {{ux|en|Why do you '''speed''' when the road is so icy?}} #* {{RQ:Salinger Catcher|page=25|passage=It had these very funny, crazy plays in it, and then it had this one story about a traffic cop that falls in love with this very cute girl that’s always '''speeding'''.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To increase the rate at which something occurs. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1982|author=Carole Offir; Carole Wade|title=Human sexuality,|publisher=Harcourt Brace Jovanovich|page=454 |passage=It is possible that the uterine contractions '''speed''' the sperm along.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=James M. Cypher; James L. Dietz|title=The process of economic development|page=359|publisher=Routledge |passage=Such interventions can help to '''speed''' the process of reducing CBRs and help countries pass through the demographic transition threshold more quickly{{nb...}}.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive|slang}} To be under the [[influence]] of stimulant drugs, especially [[amphetamine]]s. #* {{quote-song|en|title=Walk on the Wild Side|author=Lou Reed|album=Transformer|year=1972 |passage=Jackie is just '''speeding''' away / Thought she was James Dean for a day}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2008|author=Christos Tsiolkas|title=The Slap|page=46|publisher=Allen and Unwin |passage=If Hector had not been '''speeding''', it was possible that his next thought would have hurt: he loves his uncle unconditionally, in a way he will never love me.}} # {{lb|en|obsolete}} To be [[expedient]]. # {{lb|en|archaic}} To hurry to destruction; to put an end to; to ruin. #* {{RQ:Shakespeare Taming of the Shrew|act=III|scene=ii|passage= infected with the fashions, full of wingdalls, '''sped''' with spavins, rayed with yellows}} #* {{RQ:Pope Arbuthnot|lines=31–32|page=2|passage=A dire dilemma! either vvay I'm '''ſped''', / If Foes, they vvrite, if Friends, they read me dead.}} # {{lb|en|archaic}} To wish success or good fortune to, in any undertaking, especially in setting out upon a journey. #* {{RQ:Homer Pope et al Odyssey|book=XV|passage=Welcome the coming, '''speed''' the parting guest.}} # To cause to make haste; to dispatch with celerity; to drive at full speed; hence, to hasten; to hurry. #* {{RQ:Tasso Fairfax Godfrey of Bulloigne|passage=He '''sped''' him thence, home to his habitation.}} # To hasten to a conclusion; to expedite. #* {{RQ:Ayliffe Juris Canonici|passage=Judicial acts{{...}}are '''sped''' in open court at the instance of one or both of the parties.}} =====Usage notes===== * The ''Cambridge Guide to English Usage'' indicates that ''sped'' is for objects in motion ''(the race car sped)'' while ''speeded'' is used for activities or processes, but notes that the British English convention does not hold in American English. * ''Garner's Modern American Usage'' (2009) indicates that ''speeded'' is incorrect, except in the phrasal verb, {{m|en|speed up}}. Most American usage of ''speeded'' conforms to this. * ''Sped'' is about six times more common in American English ([[COCA]]) than ''speeded''. ''Sped'' is twice as common in UK English ([[BNC]]). =====Quotations===== * {{see citations|en}} =====Derived terms===== {{col|en|speed up|despeed|dispeed|forespeed|misspeed|outspeed|speeder|Godspeed}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to go fast}} * Bulgarian: * Danish: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Lithuanian: * Norwegian: * Persian: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|нести́сь|impf}}, {{t+|ru|мчаться}} * Sanskrit: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tagalog: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to exceed speed limit}} * Bulgarian: * Danish: * Dutch: * Finnish: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Norwegian: * Spanish: * Swedish: {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * Dutch: {{t+check|nl|snellen}} * Indonesian: {{t+check|id|laju|alt=melaju}} {{trans-bottom}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=deeps|pedes|deeps|Peeds|Deeps|spede}} {{C|en|Physical quantities|Mechanics}} {{cln|en|irregular verbs}}
